overview: Rehabilitation protocols authored by Physical Therapist Bruce R. Wilk: Immediate Day-1 passive range of motion, prevention of post-op adhesion recurrence, mechanical stretching devices (TheraBite), ultrasound, and isometric jaw stabilization exercises.

modules.title: Immediate Day 1 Passive Motion & Adhesion Recurrence Prevention
modules.core_concept: The most common cause of long-term failure after successful arthroscopic lysis and lavage is fibrous re-adhesion formation due to post-operative joint immobilization. Physical therapy MUST begin on Post-Operative Day 1 with gentle passive range of motion exercises.
modules.surgical_technique:
Protocol:
1) Days 1-7: Passive stretch, tongue-to-palate opening exercises, gentle lateral excursions, target vertical opening >= 35 mm.
2) Weeks 2-4: Active assisted opening, dynamic mechanical stretching (e.g. TheraBite device or tongue blade wedges), ultrasound and moist heat to masticatory muscles.
3) Weeks 4-8: Isometric strengthening of opening/closing musculature and postural correction.
modules.danger_zones_pearls: Rehab Pearl: 'Movement is medicine for synovial joints.' The surgeon must instruct the patient that mild discomfort during opening exercises is expected and necessary to prevent newly formed fibrin strands from organizing into dense collagenous scar adhesions.

challenge.scenario: A patient undergoes successful arthroscopic lysis and lavage for a severe closed lock. The surgeon instructs the patient to keep their jaw completely motionless and immobilized for 4 weeks with a soft diet and no opening exercises.
challenge.question: What is the probable negative clinical outcome of this 4-week complete joint immobilization?
options: The patient will develop an extra pair of salivary glands
Fibrin exudate will organize into dense recurrent fibrous adhesions, resulting in joint hypomobility and relapsed closed lock
The mandibular condyle will double in length
The facial nerve will become permanently paralyzed
challenge.rationale: Immobilization after joint surgery allows postoperative hematoma and fibrin exudates to organize into dense fibrous scar adhesions, causing relapsed hypomobility. Immediate passive motion is essential.

flashcards.front: When should physical therapy begin following TMJ arthroscopy?
flashcards.back: On Post-Operative Day 1 (immediate gentle passive motion).

flashcards.front: Why is joint immobilization after arthroscopy strictly contraindicated?
flashcards.back: It leads to rapid organization of fibrin into dense recurrent fibrous adhesions and joint relock.

flashcards.front: What is the early post-operative vertical mouth opening target?
flashcards.back: >= 35 to 40 mm of unassisted interincisal opening.

title: Psychological Evaluation & The TMJ Surgical Patient
author: Mark T. Frazier, Ph.D.
pdf_file: principles and practice of TMJ arthroscopy-297-301.pdf
overview: Psychological dimensions of temporomandibular disorders by Clinical Psychologist Mark T. Frazier. Somatization, secondary gain, depression, stress-induced bruxism, chronic central sensitization, and psychological screening tools (MMPI) to avoid operating on patients with somatoform pain disorders.

modules.title: Chronic Orofacial Pain, Somatization, & Surgical Gatekeeping
modules.core_concept: Chronic orofacial pain frequently involves complex psychosocial comorbidity. While surgical arthroscopy cures mechanical derangements and local synovitis, it CANNOT cure central sensitization, fibromyalgia, major depression, or somatization disorder. Patients with high scores on hypochondriasis and hysteria scales often report persistent or worsened pain after technically perfect surgery.
modules.surgical_technique: Pre-operative evaluation must include psychological screening: assess pain chronicity (>6 months), sleep disruption, widespread body pain, catastrophic thinking, and history of multiple failed surgeries. Involve a behavioral pain psychologist before scheduling invasive procedures.
modules.danger_zones_pearls: Surgeon's Golden Rule: 'Never operate on an MRI image alone.' A displaced disc in an asymptomatic individual is a normal anatomic variant in 30% of the population. A displaced disc in a patient with severe somatization may be entirely incidental to their centrally mediated chronic pain.

challenge.scenario: A 36-year-old patient presents with generalized body aches, chronic neck/back pain, sleep apnea, severe depression, and vague bilateral facial tenderness. An MRI shows mild disc displacement. The patient has had 4 previous surgeries on other body parts without relief and demands 'immediate joint surgery to cure the pain.'
challenge.question: What is the most prudent surgical recommendation?
options: Perform emergency bilateral open joint discectomy
Decline immediate surgery; refer for comprehensive multidisciplinary chronic pain and behavioral psychology management to address central sensitization
Perform an immediate bilateral eminectomy
Reassure the patient that surgery has a 100% guarantee of curing their generalized body pain
challenge.rationale: Patients with centralized chronic pain and somatization do not benefit from localized joint surgery. Operating on incidental imaging findings in these individuals often worsens symptoms and fails to address the underlying neurobiological and psychological condition.

flashcards.front: Why is psychological screening essential prior to TMJ surgery?
flashcards.back: To identify central sensitization, depression, and somatization, preventing unnecessary surgery for non-articular pain.

flashcards.front: What percentage of normal asymptomatic individuals have disc displacement on MRI?
flashcards.back: Approximately 30% of asymptomatic individuals have disc displacement.
